name: cc-toolkit
description: Claude Code plugins for spec-driven delivery, code review, manual app testing, CI and pull-request chores, walkthrough videos as pull-request proof, plan review with OpenAI Codex, research reports, transcription, naming, hook rules, and a sound when Claude waits for you

plugins.name: codex-plan-improver
plugins.description: Intercepts ExitPlanMode to automatically review implementation plans via OpenAI Codex CLI. Includes /codex-review command for manual invocation.

plugins.name: hookify
plugins.description: Easily create hooks to prevent unwanted behaviors by analyzing conversation patterns

plugins.name: session-learner
plugins.description: Analyze conversation for friction signals (corrections, repeated instructions, deviations) and interactively update project documentation (.claude/rules/, CLAUDE.md) with verified learnings. Coordinates with Claude Code's auto memory to avoid duplication.

plugins.name: namesmith
plugins.description: Business name discovery: generates candidates, challenges them with a sub-agent, then checks domain availability via Instant Domain Search MCP.

plugins.name: scribe
plugins.description: Audio/video transcription pipeline with summary, news extraction, and custom processing. Sources: YouTube URLs (yt-dlp) or local files (any format ffmpeg handles). Backed by ElevenLabs Scribe.

plugins.name: code-review
plugins.description: Unified code review that fans out parallel scanners over a change — one per active lens, up to twelve per run — and merges them into one per-file report. Twelve lenses: comment quality, four quality/craft lenses (readability & tests, naming & module, objects & patterns, simplicity & types), an always-on correctness lens (wrong conditions, unhandled cases, off-by-one, swallowed errors, races, broken call contracts), an always-on narrow security lens (secrets, injection, access checks, boundary validation, insecure settings, IaC exposure, access widening, plus access policies and CI workflows), an always-on coherence lens (docs, contracts, migrations, config and sibling listings that disagree with the code or each other, code breaking a rule an accepted ADR or CONTEXT.md states), an always-on assumptions lens (code relying on library, runtime, CI or platform behaviour the installed source or the locked version contradicts, test doubles the real dependency would not match), a performance lens for executable source (N+1, unbounded fetch, blocking-in-async, wasted renders, missing indexes), a spec lens via --spec <path> or a spec file the diff carries, and a hookify lens that replays the project's hookify rules over the diff when its .claude/ holds any. Explicit rules in a root CODING_STANDARDS.md (plus a gitignored .local.md overlay) generate standards findings. Reviews the current branch diff by default (or explicit paths / --base, or a GitHub PR with --pr). Quality findings are tagged family · rule · severity; comment verdicts are R1–R12 · KEEP/REMOVE/REWRITE/MOVE/ADD, shown side by side and applied through a single risk-cut menu.

plugins.name: researcher
plugins.description: Source-grounded research assistant: an interactive skill gathers a research brief, then launches a bundled Dynamic Workflow that fans out firecrawl retrieval (WebSearch fallback) into cited findings, gates rounds on coverage and contradictions, and renders a self-contained HTML report where every claim traces to a numbered source. The report evolves across follow-up runs.

plugins.name: tester
plugins.description: On-demand manual verification of a running app by an agent: one command discovers the live stack, builds an ephemeral environment brief, derives test suites from a spec's acceptance criteria (or the git diff), and fans out one subagent per suite across three surfaces — curl for API, agent-browser for UI, and fault-injection (dependency pause/stop or a WireMock proxy) for error handling — each returning an evidence-backed PASS/FAIL table under a hard assertion contract. The light counterpart to mt: no config, no persisted plan. User-run only.

plugins.name: fd3
plugins.description: Spec-driven delivery pipeline: grill a topic into ratified decisions, write and validate a spec against it, split the spec into dependency-ordered tasks, then implement them in isolated worktrees with batched validation.

plugins.name: dev-kit
plugins.description: Small everyday development skills: diagnose and fix failed CI pipelines, shepherd a pull request until CI is green and review is resolved, check a dependency upgrade against the codebase, and push a branch as a pull request filled from the repository's template and labelled with its risk, assessed by TypeSafe Jev, Gemini Decision or both.

plugins.name: pr-proof
plugins.description: Proof that a pull request's change works: prepare-proof judges which proof a branch needs, with signals from TypeSafe Jev or Gemini Decision when a key is set, then produces each kind, a narrated walkthrough video with playwright-recast, screenshots at the project's breakpoints, and masked terminal or API transcripts, and hands it to pr-open through the branch's proof manifest.

plugins.name: stop-sound
plugins.description: Chimes when Claude waits for you: when it finishes a turn and when it asks a question. Silent while subagents work.
